synthesis_notes.off_target_rationale: Target A share (20-25%) is unachievable in v3 — no ethnographic / field-interview source for gig workers is present in the pool. Vallas & Schor is a theoretical / literature-review paper (Grade C). Hitting A would require adding: UC Berkeley Labor Center gig-worker ethnographies, Dubal's driver-strike fieldwork, JPM Chase Institute gig-pay panel data, or CA AG deposition records. B / C / D shares are on target.

source_roles.B: fincen_2024_identity_fta (account takeover, synthetic ID fraud typologies), fincen_sar_key_terms (ATO, BEC advisories), fed_reserve_synthetic_identity_fraud (synthetic-ID definition and framework)
source_roles.C: vallas_schor_2020_gig_platforms (platform-labor structure, algorithmic control, platform list, precarity framings)
source_roles.D: design assumptions for corridor/persona detail without specific source support

personas.name: DeShawn Williams
personas.summary: DeShawn, 31, Black, Detroit. Full-time multi-apper: Uber + DoorDash + Instacart. Cashes out daily via Instant Pay ($1.99 fee). Cycles phones every 2 years because the screens crack on long shifts. His Uber account was briefly suspended in 2023 over a rating dispute — lost 4 days of income while appealing.
personas.sim_history: one SIM for 3 years, T-Mobile prepaid

platform_mix.evidence_basis: V&S: on-demand service workers cited as Uber/Lyft/DoorDash/Instacart/TaskRabbit; multi-apping is documented pattern

classification.evidence_basis: V&S: 'platforms almost always classify workers as independent contractors'; US social-insurance disconnect

earnings_volatility.evidence_basis: V&S: 'Platform workers bear all the costs of inadequate demand and lost earnings'

suspension_event_2023.value: brief Uber suspension over rating dispute

personas.name: Yuki Tanaka
personas.summary: Yuki, 38, Japanese-American, TaskRabbit + Lyft in San Francisco. A 2017-era study documented women and workers of color receiving fewer reviews and lower ratings on TaskRabbit/Fiverr — she feels this daily. Cashes out weekly to smooth income. Part-time supplementary to a graphic-design freelance practice.

rating_bias_context.value: women + workers of color rated lower on TaskRabbit/Fiverr
rating_bias_context.evidence_basis: V&S p14: Hannák et al. 2017 study of TaskRabbit and Fiverr

platform_mix.evidence_basis: V&S names all three platforms explicitly

supplementary_income.evidence_basis: V&S: many gig workers use platforms as supplement to asset monetization or other income

personas.name: Rajesh Patel
personas.summary: Rajesh, 42, Indian-origin naturalized US citizen, Chicago. Amazon Flex 5-9am weekdays before his day job; Uber Eats 6-11pm evenings. Bimodal schedule. Uses Flex's scheduled-blocks model; earnings depend on grabbing available blocks fast.
personas.daily_cashout_pattern: Amazon Flex weekly direct deposit; Uber Instant Pay occasional

platform_mix_bimodal.value: Amazon Flex mornings + Uber Eats evenings
platform_mix_bimodal.evidence_basis: V&S frames platform-worker diversity; bimodal multi-platform scheduling is documented structural pattern (joint platform+hour grounding drove v2 R3 improvements)

algorithmic_block_scarcity.value: earnings dependent on grabbing Amazon Flex blocks fast
algorithmic_block_scarcity.evidence_basis: V&S: algorithms render labor process 'legible to employers not employees'

personas.name: Ahmed Bah
personas.summary: Ahmed, 36, Senegalese-born LPR, Uber driver in Manhattan — full-time, 65hr weeks. Business Email Compromise attempt in early 2024: got a convincing email from 'Uber Driver Relations' demanding he verify his banking info; caught it because the URL was wrong. Reports trying to warn other drivers in his WhatsApp group.

personas.name: Brittany Cole
personas.summary: Brittany, 34, white, suburban Columbus Ohio. Shipt + Instacart; part-time to supplement her partner's paycheck and cover two kids' activities. Schedule-of-convenience shopper; rejects batches with bad tips. Cashout weekly.
personas.sim_history: postpaid family plan, same SIM 5+ years

supplementary_income.evidence_basis: V&S: most gig workers are NOT the precarious full-time trope; many use platforms for supplementary income

tip_stealing_era_context.evidence_basis: V&S p13: Instacart media campaign early 2019

personas.name: Hai Pham
personas.summary: Hai, 47, Vietnamese-born US citizen, owns a small nail salon in Houston but also runs DoorDash evenings to pay down the salon's 2020 COVID-era debt. Keeps two phones — one for salon clients, one for DoorDash.

all_fields.notes: Grade D — dual-role persona (small-business + gig) not specifically grounded in v3 sources

personas.name: Olumide Bakare
personas.summary: Olumide, 29, Nigerian-born on an H-2B-origin pathway (now on employment-based visa), Atlanta. Lyft + UberEats + Grubhub. Full-time driver, 55hr weeks. Multi-app to smooth slow hours.
personas.daily_cashout_pattern: daily Instant Pay across both apps

personas.name: Maria Soto
personas.summary: Maria, 33, Mexican-American, Austin. Postmates + Rover (dog-walking). Bilingual but prefers Spanish-speaking customers. Rover is her stable income; Postmates fills midday gaps. Used car, high miles.

personas.name: Tyler Brennan
personas.summary: Tyler, 24, white, Chicago, DoorDash + Uber Eats full-time. His DoorDash account was hit by a synthetic-identity attack in 2024 — attacker used his partial leaked PII to open a second driver account, route payments elsewhere. Took 3 weeks to resolve.

fraud_exposure_synthetic_id.value: synthetic ID attack on platform account 2024
fraud_exposure_synthetic_id.evidence_basis: Fed Reserve: 'combination of PII to fabricate a person or entity'; FTA_IDENTITY_2024_T13 Synthetic Identity

personas.name: Devi Reddy
personas.summary: Devi, 36, Indian-American, Philadelphia. Rover (dog-walking/boarding) primary, Care.com secondary (childcare). Fully WFH parent-friendly gig mix; caters to premium clients in Rittenhouse.

all_fields.notes: Grade D — Rover/Care.com not directly covered in V&S

personas.name: Marcus Johnson
personas.summary: Marcus, 27, Black, Detroit. DoorDash + Walmart Spark. Account taken over via credential stuffing in early 2024 using a password leaked in the 2019 Collection-1 breach. Lost 5 days' earnings; now uses a password manager and FIDO2 token.

personas.name: Alex Morgan
personas.summary: Alex, 31, white, NYC Brooklyn. TaskRabbit handyman full-time, plus occasional Uber. Furniture assembly specialist. Deep platform reliance; knows every ratings-gaming hack. Aware of the 2019 Instacart tip-stealing case and its culture-shift effect.

platform_and_rating_gaming.evidence_basis: V&S: algorithmic opacity + rating-system centrality to platform labor control

tip_stealing_case_awareness.evidence_basis: V&S p13: media campaign against Instacart early 2019
